title: List-to-search routing guard must reject RV, Name, and KeysOnly
answers: Why does an allowlisted resource list fall back to the store path instead of search?
List with ResourceVersion or a Name returns stale/wrong results when routed to search
How does the server decide whether to serve a LIST via the search index vs the revision-aware store?
body:
Symptom: a LIST for an allowlisted (or selector-bearing) resource with a non-zero ResourceVersion, a non-empty Options.Key.Name, or KeysOnly=true was returned from search and was wrong (newer-than-requested objects, every object instead of the named one, or search-specific fields on a keys-only call).
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:shouldUseSearchForList routes requests to the ResourceSearchRequest path, but that request has no RV constraint, no name filter (ListOptions contract excludes name for search), and isn't meant for keys-only lists.
Fix pattern: any list-routing decision in this function must early-return false for req.ResourceVersion > 0, req.Options.Key.Name != "", req.KeysOnly, and cross-namespace (Options.Key.Namespace == "") before considering selectors or the allowlist.
Constraints: applies to any future change that widens what goes through search-backed list (e.g. adding more allowlist entries or selector types); does not apply to Watch requests, which legitimately combine selectors with RV.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/resource list routing between search and the revision-aware store backend
says: List returns items newer than the requested version
Searching by name returns all items instead of one
Keys-only list returns complete objects instead of keys
Resource version constraints are ignored when listing
Name filter doesn't work when listing resources
search: List-to-search routing guard in shouldUseSearchForList must early-return false for req.ResourceVersion > 0, req.Options.Key.Name != "", req.KeysOnly, or cross-namespace (Options.Key.Namespace == "") before evaluating selectors or allowlist entries. Routing these cases to ResourceSearchRequest causes wrong results: non-zero RV returns newer-than-requested objects (no RV constraint in search), Name filters return every object (search lacks name filter per ListOptions contract), and KeysOnly=true gets search-specific fields. Does not apply to Watch requests which legitimately combine selectors with RV. Applies to pkg/storage/unified/resource list routing between search and the revision-aware store backend.
